rows.title: Observation-Contingent Policy-Tree Recursion

maturity_record.invariant: A finite policy-tree node equals its stage cost plus the observation-law weighted values of observation-contingent continuation trees.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Belief, action, and observation carriers are finite and the horizon is a natural-number depth. Observation laws and deterministic belief updates are supplied by the model; no infinite-horizon or continuous-belief claim is made.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: A successor node can choose different continuation trees after different observations, whereas the depth-zero carrier has exactly zero value.

rows.assumptions_and_scope: PolicyTreeModel supplies normalized observation laws, arbitrary deterministic belief updates and arbitrary real stage costs. novelty_record.carrier_delta: Replaces a fixed policy sequence with a depth-indexed, observation-contingent tree over finite belief, action, and observation carriers.

touching_relations.rationale: Observation-contingent policy-tree recursion and sophisticated-EFE backward recursion both expose finite-horizon continuation values while retaining distinct model carriers.

rows.title: Finite Policy-Tree Bellman Minimum

maturity_record.invariant: Backward induction exposes an exact finite-action Bellman minimum of stage cost plus observation-weighted optimal continuation.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The action carrier is finite and nonempty, and belief and observation carriers are finite. The result is one finite-horizon recursion, not a contraction or fixed-point theorem.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The selected action is proved no worse than every explicit alternative at each node rather than merely being named as an argmin.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep129_optimalTreeValue_eq_min and fep129_optimalTreeAction_le.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep129_optimalTreeValue_eq_min:
theorem fep129_optimalTreeValue_eq_min
    {Belief Action Observation : Type*}
    [Fintype Belief] [Fintype Action] [Fintype Observation] [Nonempty Action]
    (model : PolicyTreeModel Belief Action Observation)
    (depth : ℕ) (belief : Belief) :
    optimalTreeValue model (depth + 1) belief =
      model.stageCost depth belief (optimalTreeAction model depth belief) +
        ∑ observation,
          model.observationLaw belief (optimalTreeAction model depth belief)
              observation *
            optimalTreeValue model depth
              (model.update belief (optimalTreeAction model depth belief)
                observation)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep129_optimalTreeAction_le:
theorem fep129_optimalTreeAction_le
    {Belief Action Observation : Type*}
    [Fintype Belief] [Fintype Action] [Fintype Observation] [Nonempty Action]
    (model : PolicyTreeModel Belief Action Observation)
    (depth : ℕ) (belief : Belief) (alternative : Action) :
    model.stageCost depth belief (optimalTreeAction model depth belief) +
        ∑ observation,
          model.observationLaw belief (optimalTreeAction model depth belief)
              observation *
            optimalTreeValue model depth
              (model.update belief (optimalTreeAction model depth belief)
                observation) ≤
      model.stageCost depth belief alternative +
        ∑ observation,
          model.observationLaw belief alternative observation *
            optimalTreeValue model depth
              (model.update belief alternative observation)

rows.statement_review: finiteArgmin selects an action attaining the stage-plus-weighted-optimal-continuation objective; supporting inequality compares it to every action. This is actual finite Bellman minimization, not just an argmin name.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: Actions finite/nonempty; observation weights nonnegative normalized; belief/update/costs supplied. Stage index is remaining depth, not automatically elapsed time. Neither Bellman contraction nor infinite-horizon stationary policy is proved, and minimizers need not be unique.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: One-stage Boolean actions with costs0 and1 give selected value0 and alternative comparison; tied costs permit any minimizing action.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: An empty action type cannot meet the existence contract. Negative stage costs are allowed at finite depth and do not by themselves invalidate minimization, but no infinite-horizon boundedness follows.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 033 is deterministic discounted ENNReal rollout,071 a real sophisticated recursion.129 is finite action minimization in the explicit tree setting; current relations keep these value carriers separate.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Backward induction exposes an exact finite-action Bellman minimum at every policy-tree node.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds belief-dependent observation-weighted continuation values to the earlier scalar dynamic-programming and sophisticated-EFE recursions.

touching_relations.rationale: Exact finite-action tree minimization extends the earlier scalar Bellman recursion with belief and observation-contingent continuation structure.

rows.title: Optimal Finite Policy-Tree Existence

maturity_record.invariant: Every finite-depth, finite-carrier policy-tree problem with a nonempty action set has a concrete backward-inducted tree attaining the recursive optimum.
maturity_record.assumption_review: All carriers and the horizon are finite and the action carrier is nonempty. Existence does not extend to unbounded horizon, arbitrary measurable policy spaces, or continuous beliefs.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The witness is an actual depth-indexed tree and is compared with every other tree on the same finite carrier.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep130_exists_optimalPolicyTree and fep130_policyTree_carrier_finite.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep130_exists_optimalPolicyTree:
theorem fep130_exists_optimalPolicyTree
    {Belief Action Observation : Type*}
    [Fintype Belief] [Fintype Action] [Fintype Observation] [Nonempty Action]
    (model : PolicyTreeModel Belief Action Observation)
    (depth : ℕ) (belief : Belief) :
    ∃ tree : PolicyTree Action Observation depth,
      policyTreeValue model tree belief = optimalTreeValue model depth belief ∧
        ∀ alternative : PolicyTree Action Observation depth,
          policyTreeValue model tree belief ≤
            policyTreeValue model alternative belief

rows.statement_review: The recursively built optimalPolicyTree attains optimalTreeValue and is below every alternative at equal finite depth. Tree carrier finiteness is separately established. This is a real attaining existence result.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: Construction is noncomputable finiteArgmin/classical choice, not a certified efficient executable planner. No uniqueness, infinite-depth optimum, complete continuous-belief simplex enumeration or empirical plan adequacy follows. The theorem does not just assert a supplied optimum.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: For boolFeedbackModel at depth2, the explicit feedback tree value0 and nonnegative mismatch cost provide a nontrivial attaining minimum; generic theorem compares all same-depth trees.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Tied action costs allow multiple distinct optimal trees. Unbounded horizon with negative per-step costs has no finite real minimum promised by this theorem.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 008 is a fixed finite one-step argmin;130 lifts finite selection through every observation branch and compares all finite trees.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Every finite-depth policy-tree problem with a nonempty finite action carrier has a concrete attaining optimal tree.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Lifts one finite argmin to an explicitly finite depth-indexed tree constructed by backward induction.

touching_relations.rationale: A concrete attaining finite policy tree is paired with the original finite policy minimizer, making the stronger depth-indexed carrier and its nonempty-action premise explicit.

rows.title: Open-Loop Plan Embedding into Policy Trees

maturity_record.invariant: Reusing the same continuation after every observation embeds an open-loop action plan into the policy-tree carrier without changing its recursive value.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The comparison uses the same model, belief, and finite depth. Open-loop plans ignore observations by construction; the theorem does not identify arbitrary state-feedback policies with open-loop sequences.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: At positive depth the embedding duplicates a common continuation across all observation branches; at depth zero both carriers reduce to their unique leaf.

rows.statement_review: OpenLoopPlan embeds by reusing one continuation across all observation branches; its recursive value equals the corresponding tree value at the same model, belief and depth.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: Actions ignore observation history, but the model's belief update and expectation still follow observations during evaluation; open-loop does not mean freeze belief. Same-depth/model hypotheses matter.

rows.title: Closed-Loop Policy-Tree Dominance over Open Loop

maturity_record.invariant: The optimal observation-contingent finite policy tree is no worse than every open-loop plan embedded at the same depth.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Actions are finite and nonempty, all other carriers are finite, and both sides share one finite horizon and cost model. No infinite-horizon POMDP dominance is claimed.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The strict Boolean witness in fep-134 demonstrates that the inequality can be strict rather than only equality under an observation-irrelevant model.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep132_optimalTree_le_openLoop with an arbitrary same-depth open-loop plan.

rows.statement_review: The globally minimizing finite tree is no worse than any value-preserving embedded same-depth open-loop plan. This follows from inclusion of that plan in the larger policy class.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: This is weak dominance for one cost/observation/update model; strict advantage is possible, not universal. Finitely many actions and finite horizon remain; the depth<depth+1 supporting theorem merely records natural-depth arithmetic and adds no planning evidence.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Use134 to show0<1/2 strict advantage for the explicit feedback example.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: At depth0, constant costs or observation-irrelevant continuation, equality holds. Altering model/horizon between sides breaks the comparison guarantee.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 071 also had finite feedback-vs-fixed-plan content;132 now has a universal same-depth plan embedding/optimal-tree dominance, not an infinite-horizon POMDP claim.

novelty_record.new_invariant: The optimal finite closed-loop policy-tree value is no greater than every embedded same-depth open-loop plan value.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Turns the open-loop embedding into a finite-horizon dominance theorem and leaves infinite-horizon POMDP optimality outside scope.

touching_relations.rationale: Closed-loop tree optimality dominates every embedded open-loop plan, while fep-071 supplies the earlier two-stage feedback-sensitive EFE recursion.

maturity_record.non_vacuity: The induction ranges over observation-contingent continuations and the optimal-value theorem compares independently constructed minimizing trees.

rows.title: Strict Boolean Feedback Advantage

maturity_record.invariant: In the explicit two-step Boolean model, observation-contingent feedback has value zero while every fixed open-loop second action has value one half.
maturity_record.assumption_review: This is a finite exact counterexample on fair Boolean observations and a mismatch terminal cost. It demonstrates possible feedback advantage, not a universal quantitative gap for active-inference agents.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The continuation action provably differs between false and true observations and the strict gap is exactly one half.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of fep134_boolFeedback_strictlyBetter and fep134_feedback_continuation_changes with both Boolean actions.

rows.statement_review: The concrete depth2 Bool feedback continuation changes its second action with the first observation, giving value0 against1/2 for each fixed second action in boolOpenLoopPlan. This is exact nonvacuous possible feedback advantage.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The fair first observation and terminal mismatch objective are authored; generic boolFeedbackModel is a supplied belief/update model. Existing boolBayes_rederives_feedbackWitness separately realizes the same values via an actual finite Bayesian filter, with support/scope specific to that construction. rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: If observation conveys no useful variable for terminal cost or both actions have equal cost, strict feedback advantage disappears. A keep-prior update fails the delivered Bayes agreement control.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 071 supplied feedback example is a neighbor;134 owns the explicit tree and continuation-change fact. The Bayesian perception-action foundation adds a substantive actual carrier bridge without proving empirical benefit.

findings.finding: The generic full-support EFE model still permits arbitrary belief updates; the existing Bayesian specialization should be named separately.
findings.proposed_text: Every belief-indexed generative model satisfies FullSupport and supplies actual model-derived EFE, risk and ambiguity. The generic update is an arbitrary function and need not be the preceding model's Bayesian posterior. The separate BayesianBeliefModel/update_filtered specialization and its policy-tree/POMDP/risk-ambiguity bridges establish that stronger filtered interpretation under their explicit support premises. All horizons/carriers remain finite; empirical adequacy is not established.
